subject: Reserved capacity tenor, ramp schedule, and throughput guarantees — SprintBridge
messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@sprintbridge.com>
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: contracts@sprintbridge.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial sizing + questions on reserved capacity tenor and guarantees

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the sizing worksheet (attached) with infra and product. A few items we need clarified before procurement can move forward:

- Our projected steady-state is roughly 120k tokens/minute (peak bursts ~210k) for the first 6 months; we believe this maps to ~6 x A100-class GPU pool, but we want Redwood's sizing confirmation and how you map that to dedicated "slots" vs. pooled vGPU capacity.
- Term options: procurement prefers 24 months but will consider 12 or 36 if pricing/tiering is favorable. What sort of discount ladder do you offer across 12/24/36 months and across committed throughput tiers?
- Ramp schedule / activation: we need a clear start date window (we're targeting Oct 1, 2027), phased activation milestones, and any credit or pro-rating mechanics if our usage ramps slower.
- Throughput guarantees / SLOs: what measurable per-route throughput or p99 generation latency guarantees apply to Dedicated? Any remedies or credit structure for missed targets?

I've attached our sizing worksheet and a high-level expected month-by-month ramp. Would appreciate a written summary we can attach to our procurement package.

Would you be able to propose one or two concrete term/discount options and an activation timeline we can review with procurement this week?

Thanks,
Alex Porter
VP Product, SprintBridge
attachments: SprintBridge_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@sprintbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing + questions on reserved capacity tenor and guarantees

Alex —

Appreciate the detailed worksheet. Quick answers up front, and then a concrete proposal below.

Sizing: based on the token flow and burst profile you shared, our recommendation is a dedicated pool mapped to 8 physical GPUs with dynamic vGPU packing to handle spikes (6 GPUs sustained / 2 GPUs burst headroom). That gives you headroom for +20–30% burst without immediate autoscaling events. We'll provide a lines-of-code-to-tokens mapping and a short runbook for how we size model variants vs. capacity.

Term & discount framework (high level):
- 12 months: base rate, minimal discount (reference price).
- 24 months: mid-tier discount (~12–16% off base) with a 10% staging credit if activation is >30 days after contract effective date.
- 36 months: deepest discount (~20–25%) plus guaranteed price lock and a 30% transient credit for the first 2 months if activation is staggered.

Ramp & start dates: we can target Oct 1, 2027 as your activation window. Typical structure we use: a 30-day activation window (Oct 1–Nov 1) with two milestone checkpoints — "soft activation" (capacity available for testing, no heavy production) and "go live" (full production routing). If go live slips, we pro-rate billing until the go-live date and apply the staging credit described above for eligible terms.

Throughput guarantees: for Dedicated pools we offer throughput SLOs tied to committed GPU capacity. For your proposed pool (8 GPUs):
- Sustained throughput floor: token/sec floor equivalent to the sizing worksheet at 95% of measured baseline.
- Latency: p95 generation latency targets per model family (listed in the formal SLA).
- Remedies: service credits up to 10% of the monthly invoice for repeated miss against SLOs over a rolling 30-day window; higher contractual remedies require legal review.

Concrete proposals (pick one):
A) 24-month plan (preferred): commit to 8 GPU pool (billing units: reserved GPU-hours) — 14% discount on per-token price; 10% staging credit if production start >30 days after effective date. 30-day activation window with two milestones.
B) 36-month plan: commit to 8 GPU pool — 22% discount; price lock for term; 20% transient credit first 60 days if activation staggered across more than one month.
C) 12-month plan: commit to 6 GPU pool (lower sustained) — 6% discount; can add burst credit top-up purchase.

I'll loop in Naomi (ops) and Marissa (account lead) to land the exact numbers and prepare the draft Master SA / SOW for your procurement. If Oct 1 is critical, call out any immovable constraints on your side; we can align staff to meet a tighter activation next quarter.

Proposed next step: short call Wednesday 10:00 PT to walk the pricing table and agree on term/activation. Is that workable?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Sizing_Notes.pdf (internal)

From: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@sprintbridge.com>, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Pricing table and draft SA (SB-2027-042)

Alex / Ben —

Following Ben's note, attaching a short pricing table and the Draft_Master_SA_v2.docx for procurement review. Key commercials below (numbers illustrative; final figures will be in the SOW):

Pricing summary (monthly equivalent) — committed 8 GPU pool:
- 12-month: $225,000/mo (base) — effective per-token multiplier 1.00 (no staging credit)
- 24-month: $193,500/mo — 14% off base; 10% staging credit if go-live >30d
- 36-month: $175,500/mo — 22% off base; 20% transient credit first 60d if staggered activation

Billing and credits:
- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears.
- Staging credit mechanics: if production go-live occurs after the 30-day activation window, the agreed staging credit is applied to the next invoice once go-live completes.
- Under-utilization: we provide a one-time buffer of 15% of committed throughput for months 1–3; persistent under-utilization will be reviewed after month 4 and may trigger re-sizing conversations.

SLA snapshot (excerpt):
- Throughput guarantee: committed GPU pool will sustain the throughput profile in your sizing worksheet at 95% availability (measured at the route level).
- Latency SLO: model family p95 targets as listed in Appendix A of the SA.
- Credit: repeated missed SLOs >3 incidents in a 30-day rolling window = credit up to 10% of that month's invoice.

Attachments included: Draft_Master_SA_v2.docx (contract language with remedies and activation milestones), SprintBridge_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx (your sheet, updated with our recommended GPU mapping).

Next steps: if the 24-month option looks good, we can update the SA with the selected term and send via DocuSign for signature (link below). If procurement requires PO-first, please indicate PO arrival timeline and we can start the internal activation process in parallel.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/SB-2027-042
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765

Thanks — happy to hop on a call today/Wednesday.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
attachments: Draft_Master_SA_v2.docx, Pricing_Table_SB-2027-042.pdf

From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@sprintbridge.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: contracts@sprintbridge.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing table and draft SA (SB-2027-042)

Naomi / Ben —

Thanks — the 24-month option looks like the right balance for us. A couple of quick asks before we route to procurement:

1) Can we move the activation window to Oct 15–Nov 15 instead of Oct 1–Nov 1? Our infra onboarding calendar slipped a bit. Per your note, that should still be in scope for the 10% staging credit, correct?
2) For the SLA credit calc, can you clarify whether the 10% credit is applied to the entire invoice or to the affected route only? Procurement prefers route-level credits.
3) We'll need the final SA with the 24-month term and the 8 GPU pool line item to attach to the PO request. If you can send the DocuSign with those edits, procurement can turn around a PO in ~7 business days.

Assuming the above are OK, we're ready to move forward. Happy to take the Wednesday 10:00 PT call if helpful.

Cheers,
Alex
VP Product — SprintBridge
